h1:
Trang Street Food & Morning Markets
An Old-Town Food Walk
intro: Trang is a town that wakes up early to eat. People here start the day with dim sum and a glass of kopi before the sky is fully light, then keep going through a morning market packed with crispy-skin roast pork, khanom jeen noodles, Chinese doughnuts and local sweets. This is a walking guide to Trang's old town the way locals actually eat it, with shop names, neighborhoods and the prices you'll see right now.

blocks.html: If there's one town in Thailand where breakfast is taken as seriously as a ritual, Trang is it. The Hokkien Chinese culture that came in with trade means a local morning revolves around a dim sum table, a glass of kopi and a plate of crispy-skin roast pork. Most of the food clusters in the old town around Thap Thiang, all within walking distance, so you don't need to drive far. We've picked out both the long-running shops and the morning market you should hit in a single trip.

blocks.text: Start the morning with dim sum and roast pork

blocks.html: Trang dim sum is nothing like the mall version in Bangkok. Here it's served at tae tiam (old-school coffee shops), one hot steamer basket at a time — order as much as you want and they count what you eat. It pairs with Trang roast pork, where the skin is crispy and the meat runs sweet first, salty after. This is what locals take out-of-towners to eat before anything else.

items.name: Trang Moo Yang
items.blurb: A legendary shop locals treat as the breakfast landmark. The star is the crispy-skin roast pork — sweet and salty in balance — eaten alongside dim sum, khanom jeen with crab curry and kopi-o. Old-school room with a throwback feel, plus fried spring rolls that are hard to find elsewhere.
items.meta: Breakfast–late morning · Thap Thiang old town
items.price: Small roast pork plate around ฿120 · dim sum ฿20–30 per basket

items.name: Kopi Sathani
items.blurb: An old-school tae tiam right by Trang railway station, serving hot fresh dim sum, rice soup, pan-fried eggs and shrimp dumplings with old-style coffee hot or iced. A handy stop before or after the train.
items.price: Dim sum ฿25 per basket · under ฿100 per person

items.name: Lao Trang 2
items.blurb: A big dim sum spot with fried snacks and rice soup all in one place, open late into the evening — rare for Trang dim sum. Good for late risers or anyone who wants dim sum for dinner.
items.meta: Open 06:00–21:00 · Soi Sai Ngam 1, Thap Thiang

items.name: Sinchewy
items.blurb: A morning shop in front of the former Chaloem Trang cinema, known for dim sum, rice soup, pork-blood soup and hot fresh Chinese doughnuts. This is where working folks stop before clocking in.

items.name: Ruean Thai Dim Sum
items.blurb: Many kinds of dim sum in a spacious, comfortable room. Good for groups or families who want to order a spread and share.
items.meta: Morning–midday · Ploen Phithak Road, Thap Thiang

items.name: Pong Ocha
items.blurb: An old morning shop serving dim sum alongside charcoal-grilled roast pork — you get that traditional charcoal-smoke aroma. Opens very early and often sells out fast.
items.meta: Open 05:00–12:00 · Huai Yot Road, Thap Thiang

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Many Trang dim sum shops sell out before noon. If you want a standout like Sinchewy or Pong Ocha, go before 9am. Late risers should head straight to Lao Trang 2, which stays open longer.

blocks.text: Walk the Trang municipal morning market

blocks.html: The Trang municipal fresh market in Thap Thiang is the heart of morning grazing. It opens from around 5–6am, with food tucked along the lanes and on push-carts. Come at first light for the liveliest scene — locals and travelers both, gentle prices. You can walk in empty-handed, but carry cash since most stalls don't take transfers.

items: Trang roast pork (Ko Pao) — the market's go-to, crispy skin and sweet-salty meat, open from 06:00. Take it away or eat it with khanom jeen noodles.
Khanom jeen with nam ya / crab curry — several carts and stalls in the market, doused in punchy southern-Thai sauce and eaten with fresh raw veg on the side.
Chinese doughnuts, fried wontons, spring rolls — morning fried snacks to go with your kopi, fried fresh and hot, starting at just a few baht.
Grilled pork with sticky rice, crab noodles, fried chicken — one-plate eats brought to the street by home cooks.
Local sweets — Thai-Chinese desserts, mashed taro, beans and various pot-cooked sweets to finish off breakfast.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: The morning market has no pretty seating — it's genuinely stalls and push-carts. Some things sell out fast and shops close before midday. The charm is in the freshness, the low prices and seeing how Trang lives in the morning. Show up after 10am and you'll find fewer options left.

Kopi is Hokkien-style old-school coffee, brewed strong through a cloth sock and drunk with dim sum or kaya toast. It's a tae tiam coffee-shop culture that's still very much alive in Trang. Sipping kopi in an old shop in the morning is an experience that's hard to find in other towns.

items.name: Kopi Sathani
items.blurb: An old-school shop next to the railway station — kopi hot or iced with dim sum, in an open-front shophouse. Good to open or close out the day.

items.name: Tae tiam shops in the old town
items.blurb: The Thap Thiang area still has old-school coffee shops scattered around — wander the lanes and find them yourself. Each one has its own kopi recipe.

blocks.text: Sweets and souvenirs to close the trip

blocks.html: Before you leave, stop for Trang cake — the one locals call the cake with a hole. It's soft and buttery, originally from Huai Yot district, and these days comes in more than 20 flavors to take home.

items: Tha Pap Cake — the shop in front of the pink building on the Trang–Phatthalung road, known for coconut cake and Trang cake in many flavors. Open daily except Wednesday.
Other Trang cake shops in town — souvenir shops around Thap Thiang carry the cake-with-a-hole from several makers, so taste and compare before you buy a batch to take home.
Roast pork to go — many market stalls pack roast pork in a bag to take away. It's a souvenir locals like to carry on the plane.

blocks.html: Trang's food clusters in Thap Thiang, almost all within walking distance. Here's an eating plan that gets you a wide range without leaving you over-full in a single sitting.

items.activity: Start at Trang Moo Yang — order crispy-skin roast pork with dim sum and kopi-o.
items.note: Go early to dodge the line

items.activity: Walk the Trang municipal fresh market and try khanom jeen with crab curry and fried snacks.
Sip kopi at a tae tiam in the old town and give your stomach a break before the next meal.
Stroll the old town, stop to photograph the old buildings and pick up souvenirs.
Try Sinchewy or Pong Ocha — dim sum with hot fresh Chinese doughnuts.
Late riser? Head to Lao Trang 2, which stays open long — order fried snacks and rice soup.
Stop by Tha Pap Cake or a Trang cake shop in town and buy the cake-with-a-hole to take home.
Wrap up the trip with khanom jeen or one-plate crab noodles before you move on.

faq.q: What time does Trang's morning market open and where is it?
faq.a: The Trang municipal fresh market is in Thap Thiang, Mueang district, open from around 5 to 6am. The food is liveliest at first light, and many stalls start closing after 10am, so come early and carry cash.

faq.q: Where's the best Trang roast pork?
faq.a: The legendary spot is Trang Moo Yang in the Thap Thiang old town. In the morning market, Ko Pao does the crispy-skin, sweet-salty version — a small roast pork plate runs around ฿120, and you can also get it packed to take home as a souvenir.

faq.q: Which Trang dim sum shop opens a bit later?
faq.a: Most Trang dim sum sells out before noon. If you're a late riser, go to Lao Trang 2, which stays open into the evening. Sinchewy and Pong Ocha open very early and sell out fast, so go before 9am.

faq.q: What is kopi and how is it different from regular coffee?
faq.a: Kopi is Hokkien-style old-school coffee, brewed strong through a cloth sock — heavier than fresh-brewed coffee. It's usually drunk with dim sum or kaya toast, part of the tae tiam coffee-shop culture you can still find in Trang town.

faq.q: What food should I buy to take home from Trang?
faq.a: Trang cake — the cake-with-a-hole — is the popular souvenir: soft, buttery and in many flavors, from well-known shops like Tha Pap Cake. Packed Trang roast pork is also a popular thing to carry home.
